title: WCC - Haulage of Food Waste from Warwickshire County Council Collection Points
description:
Warwickshire County Council (the Council) was seeking a Supplier who could provide a haulage service for separately collected food waste from specified collection points. Full details were outlined in the ITT

The value of £1.8 million at II.1.7 is an anticipated figure to allow for volumes of food waste tonnage across all waste collection authorities in Warwickshire. Currently food waste is only collected separately by Warwick District and Stratford-on-Avon District.  

The initial contract term will be for a period of 2 years.
However, the Council reserves the right to extend the contract by further periods not exceeding 30 months (2 years and 6 months) in total (30 months being the maximum available extension period) at the discretion of the Council. This means the maximum possible Contract term is 4 years and 6 months in total. 

Warwickshire County Council (the Council) was seeking a Supplier who could provide a collection and haulage service for separately collected food waste stored in containers from specified collection points to the Delivery Point. Full details were outlined in the ITT.

Warwickshire County Council is the Waste Disposal Authority and managed the Council's statutory obligation to provide treatment and disposal for municipal waste collected throughout Warwickshire by the Waste Collection Authorities and/or by suppliers acting on behalf of these Councils.

The Waste Collection Authorities (WCAs) in Warwickshire are: 
North Warwickshire Borough Council;
Nuneaton and Bedworth Borough Council;
Rugby Borough Council;
Warwick District Council;
Stratford-on-Avon District Council.

The WCAs listed above have a statutory obligation to arrange for the kerbside collection of waste from households in Warwickshire.

Warwick District Council and Stratford-on-Avon District Council carry out weekly collections of separately collected food waste.

There is currently no separately collected food waste service operating in North Warwickshire Borough Council, Nuneaton and Bedworth Borough Council and Rugby Borough Council. However, it is possible that North Warwickshire Borough Council, Nuneaton and Bedworth Borough Council and Rugby Borough Council implement separate food waste collections in the near future if this is made a requirement by Government or for other reasons. If separate food waste collections are implemented by one or all of these WCAs, the Council may require a collection and haulage service for this material. Details were outlined in the ITT. These additional services will not necessarily run for the full term of the contract (4 years and 6 months) and will instead run on a co-terminus basis with the services for Warwick District Council and Stratford-on-Avon District Council.

title: WCC Recovery or disposal of municipal residual waste
description:
Warwickshire County Council ("the Council") is the Waste Disposal Authority ("WDA") for the county of Warwickshire and manages the Council's statutory obligation to provide recovery and disposal for municipal waste collected by the Waste Collection Authorities ("WCAs") and/or by suppliers acting on behalf of these Councils. 

The Waste Collection Authorities in Warwickshire are:
•	North Warwickshire Borough Council
•	Nuneaton and Bedworth Borough Council
•	Rugby Borough Council
•	Warwick District Council
•	Stratford-on-Avon District Council

The WCAs listed above have a statutory obligation to arrange for the kerbside collection of waste from households in Warwickshire. They also provide trade waste services and collect fly tipping. 

Waste materials are managed in line with the Warwickshire Joint Municipal Waste Management Strategy, the Resources and Waste Strategy for England and in compliance with the waste hierarchy and all appropriate legislation.

The Council are seeking a supplier for the recovery or disposal contract for municipal residual waste arising in Warwickshire. Applicants will be required to submit a bid to provide adequate reprocessing capacity at a site (or sites) and to accept deliveries of municipal residual waste. It is envisaged the "Contract Waste" (meaning municipal waste to be treated or disposed of under the Contract awarded) will mainly comprise municipal waste arising from Rugby Borough and Warwickshire operated household waste recycling centres ("HWRCs") (principally, Hunters Lane HWRC in Rugby) see Annex A for a map and addresses of the HWRCs. Where a WCA is required to deliver Contract Waste outside of its administrative area/zone, the Council will incur additional costs and as such the total life-cycle cost of the service will be considered within this exercise. 

Warwickshire County Council will be using its e-tendering system (In-Tend) for the administration of this procurement process and providers must register with the system to be able to express an interest.

The web address is: www.csw-jets.co.uk

Registration and use of In-Tend is free. Once registered, all correspondence for this procurement process must be via the in-tend correspondence function. However, if you are unable to register with the website please email us at procurement@warwickshire.gov.uk

During the course of the contract period the range and scope of these services may be subject to modification and variation to meet the changing needs and requirements of the Council, potential changes in legislation and the changing demands placed on the Council by its customers.

title: WCC - Reprocessing of Separately Collected Food Waste
description:
Warwickshire County Council is a waste disposal authority and is seeking to appoint a Supplier for the reprocessing of separately collected Food Waste.

The initial contract term will be for a period of 5 years. However, the Council reserves the right to extend the Contract by further periods not exceeding 60 months (5 years) in total. The maximum contract term will be 120 months (10 years). 

The Council is procuring the following lots/options:
• Lot 1 - Reprocessing of separately collected Food Waste for the whole of the Warwickshire County (all five Warwickshire Waste Collection Authorities);
• Lot 2 - Reprocessing of separately collected Food Waste from the following two Waste Collection Authorities - Warwick District Council and Stratford-on-Avon District Council;
• Lot 3 - Reprocessing of separately collected Food Waste from the following three Waste Collection Authorities - North Warwickshire Borough Council, Nuneaton and Bedworth Borough Council and Rugby Borough Council.

Please note that there is currently no separately collected Food Waste service  operating in North Warwickshire Borough Council, Nuneaton and Bedworth Borough Council and Rugby Borough Council. Therefore please note Lot 3 and the additional services in Lot 1 will not necessarily be a 10 year contract and will run on a co-terminus basis with the services for Warwick District Council and Stratford-on-Avon District Council from the point at which it starts.

All applicants must tender for all 3 Lots/options.
For the avoidance of doubt, if an applicant doesn't submit a tender for all 3 of the Lots/Options, their submission will be rejected and will not proceed to evaluation.

It is the Council's preference to award to a single Supplier via Lot 1/Option 1 for the reprocessing of food waste for the whole of Warwickshire; however, the Council reserve the right to award the Contract as two separate Lots/Options (Lot/Option 2)and (Lot/Option 3)) at its absolute sole discretion. This may be for reasons(including but not limited to) that the awarding of this Contract as two separate Lots/Options provides significantly better value to the Council in terms of the overall annual service cost compared to Lot/Option 1. However, even where this is the case, bidders are reminded that our preference is to award Lot 1/Option 1, and the Council's decision will be final.
Further detail can be found in the ITT.

title: WCC - Container provision, haulage and reprocessing of Wood Waste from Warwickshire Household Waste Recycling Centres
description:
Warwickshire County Council (the Council) is seeking a Supplier who can provide containers, along with a haulage and reprocessing service for Wood Waste from specified Warwickshire Household Waste Recycling Centres (HWRCs). Full details provided in the ITT.

It is the responsibility of Warwickshire County Council, as the Waste Disposal Authority to provide HWRCs for members of the public. The Waste Collection Authorities in Warwickshire are as follows: Warwick District Council, Stratford-on-Avon District Council, North Warwickshire Borough Council, Nuneaton and Bedworth Borough Council, Rugby Borough Council.

The waste from the HWRCs needs to be managed safely and in line with the waste hierarchy. The Council manages 8 of its HWRCs in-house and must have contracts in place for the reuse, recycling, recovery or disposal of waste materials brought to the site by the public or traders. One of the waste materials the Council needs to have a contract for is Wood Waste. In 2022/23 the amount of Wood Waste arising from all 9 Warwickshire HWRCs was approximately 8,000 tonnes (approximately 6,500 tonnes was from 8 of the Warwickshire operated HWRCs and approximately 1,500 was from Judkins HWRC). Wood Waste arising from Judkins HWRC located in Nuneaton, is operated by FCC Environment Limited ("FCC") and the reprocessing may or may not be included in the contract at the discretion of FCC and consent of the Council. If it is included, they do not require the provision of containers or haulage. 

The initial contract term will be for a period of 3 years.
However, the Council reserves the right to extend the contract by further periods not exceeding 48 months (4 years) in total at the discretion of the Council.

title: Hire of Coaches & Minibuses to the Royal Hospital Chelsea
description:
Royal Hospital Chelsea
Coach & Minibus Hire Statement of Requirement


1.	Statement of  Requirement

The Royal Hospital Chelsea requires the hiring of Coaches and Minibuses on an as required basis. The requirement is to support in the region of 300 veteran soldiers who attend various functions throughout the country. There will be occasions when coaches are required for overseas trips to mainland Europe on Battlefield tours etc. 

2.	Scope of service

The following is a list of the services required.

•	Provide liveried vehicles which are well maintained.
•	Provide a range of vehicles from 8 seats to 52 seats. The larger vehicles are to be fitted with a toilet.
•	Provide a wheelchair accessible vehicle on certain occasions.
•	Provide a driver who is well turned out.
•	Drivers should be mindful of their passengers.
•	Drivers should report 5 mins before the departure time.
•	Once passengers are set down they should not be left until they have been met.
•	Vehicles may be required for overseas and overnight trips.
•	Vehicles should be available within 12 hours.
•	There should be no cancellation charge if more than 48 hours' notice is given. 
•	All invoices to be paid by Mastercard, with no transaction fees applied.

3.	Regular bookings

Listed below are some areas where vehicles may be expected to travel:

•	Stamford Bridge. 8 seat, 20 trips per season. Duration 4 hours
•	Westminster Abbey. 33 seat, once per year. Duration 3 hours
•	Cenotaph 49 seat coach, once per year. Duration 4 hours
•	Bowls team away games 10-12 trips per year. Duration 4-8 hours 
•	Fishing Trips away. 8 seats. Approximately 25 trips a year. Duration 6-8 hours
•	G-Tech Stadium, Brentford, London Irish Rugby. 14 seats. Approximately 20 trips per year. Duration 5-6 hours. 
•	Royal Albert Hall 16 seat twice a year

title: Provision of Leicestershire Holiday Activities and Food Programme - Holiday Clubs
description:
Leicestershire County Council (the Council) is conducting a procurement to establish a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) in accordance with the Light-Touch Regime requirements of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015.\r
\r
The Council is inviting Providers to join the Leicestershire Holiday Activities and Food (HAF) Programme DPS to supply holiday club places to children resident in Leicestershire who are eligible to receive benefits-related free school meals. HAF holiday provision is for school aged children from reception to year 11 (inclusive).\r
\r
The offer of free HAF holiday club provision will be available to all Leicestershire children in receipt of benefits-related free school meals. However, it is not expected that all eligible children will take up the offer of HAF holiday club places as attendance is voluntary.\r
\r
We are seeking provision to be delivered across the County and particularly targeting areas of greatest need. The holiday clubs will take place during the Easter, Summer and Christmas school holidays.\r
\r
Holiday club provision must provide each child with; a healthy meal; engaging and enriching activities; opportunities to be physically active; nutritional education. Provision must also ensure that each child's family develop their understanding of health and nutrition, and are signposted towards other information and support, for example, health, employment, and education.\r
\r
The DPS will run for an in initial period of 2 years and 2 months from 1st November 2022 with the potential to extend in yearly increments for up to three years.\r
\r
Providers can submit an application to join the DPS at any time during the life of the DPS. The deadline for receipt of applications for Round 1 of the DPS is 12:00 12th September 2022. Once a DPS round is closed, the next round will automatically open to receive further applications until the end of the DPS.\r

description:
NHS Arden and Greater East Midlands Commissioning Support Unit on behalf of NHS Birmingham & Solihull Integrated Care Board (ICB) ("the Commissioner") notified the market of the opportunity to provide primary medical services (APMS) at Hodge Hill Family Practice.

The service commencement date is 01st April 2024. The contract is for a period of 7 years with an option to extend for a further 2 years. Based on the current contract it is anticipated that the service provision resultant of this procurement will have an annual agreement value of circa £663,037 per annum (excluding VAT) this is based on global sum of £118.76 (GMS+15%) x5,583 (6,179 raw list size) weighted list as of 01st September 2023. Please note this figure is excluding Out of Hours (OOH) deduction at 4.75% and payments for Enhanced Services, PCN Engagement and QOF. Future years will reflect any nationally agreed uplifts, updated patient list sizes etc.

This procurement was advertised in accordance with the requirements of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 (as amended) (the "Regulations") to the extent that the Regulations relate to services within the scope of Schedule 3 there to (Social and Other Specific Services). The Commissioner and AGCSU are therefore, bound only by those parts of the Regulations applying to Schedule 3 services.
